title.narrative: Health Systems Strengthening through PBF In Jimma Zone Phase II

description.narrative: A total of 3,735,524 people living in the catchment area of the 130 targeted Health Facilities in the 21 project Woredas will benefit from the project implementation.

General Objective: “Improved availability and accessibility of good quality healthcare at primary and secondary level in the Jimma Zone (Oromia Region, Ethiopia), and a stronger health system at large, which supports the progressive realization of Universal Health Coverage (SDG 3.8) in this geographical area.”

In Ethiopia, Cordaid started the phase 1 showcase project of Performance Based Financing (PBF) in the arid and pastoralist Borana Zone in 2015 which ended on the 30th of June 2018. As confirmed by an external project evaluation done in November 2018, the project contributed to an increase in both the utilization and the quality of healthcare services in Borana. With the success, Cordaid mobilized additional internal funding to implement the second phase of the project which was jointly designed by the Borana Zonal Health Department (ZHD), Cordaid and the Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) resulting in a scale-up from 4 to 8 Borana woredas, from 9 to 25 health facilities and from a catchment population of 125,918 to a population of 488,556. In March 2018, the FMOH and Cordaid organized a PBF workshop in Bishoftu during which results and lessons from the Borana case were shared and discussed. Representatives of the FMOH, ORHB, ZHD, EHIA, and Cordaid participated. Participants expressed the wish to bring PBF to a part of the Oromia region which relies mostly on sedentary farming, to also generate evidence about the impact of PBF in a non-pastoralist context. This resulted in the development of a four-year proposal to the Royal Netherlands Embassy to scale up PBF in the Jimma Zone in Oromia. The Jimma proposal was approved by the Embassy in early April 2019 and started the implementation of its six-month inception phase on the 1st of April 2019.
The Jimma PBF phase I was started on the 1st of April 2019 with a six-month inception phase and full-blown implementation was started in September 2019 at 13 Districts within respective 65 Health centres and 3 Hospitals. From January 2021, the project covers 100% of the Health Facilities in Jimma: 8 districts, 57 health centers, and 5 Hospitals, at the later stage of the project 536 Health posts have been also included in the project. The Jimma PBF has led to substantial improvement in health service utilization, access to essential quality health services, and the reliability of the data. The overall Jimma PBF project has covered, 21 woredas, 122 health centers, 536 Health posts, 5 Primary Hospitals, 3 General Hospitals, and 118 Community-Based Organizations which ensures a 3,722,559 population served both directly and indirectly. This project is a 3 year project which is a continuation of the 4 year Health System Strengthening project that was being implemented in Jimma.
